title: Geometric data and Hilbert-completion specifications for elliptic Sobolev realization
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], use smooth real manifolds [def-sfb-smooth-real-manifold], smooth finite-rank real bundles [def-sfb-smooth-real-vector-bundle] and their smooth sections [def-sfb-smooth-bundle-sections]. For a compact oriented smooth $m$-manifold $N$ without boundary, give a smooth positive Riemannian metric, a finite oriented chart cover and a positive smooth volume form, encoded as a positive smooth multiple of metric volume. Give each rank-$r$ bundle $B$ a smooth positive fibre metric. A localization is a finite family of compatible charts with smooth bundle trivializations and a smooth partition of unity whose compact supports lie in those charts. Define the order-$k$ energy of a smooth section as the sum of the squared Euclidean $L^2$ norms of every localized frame-component derivative of order at most $k$; derivatives use multi-indices in $\mathbf N^m$. Define the integrated pairing by $\int_N\langle s,t\rangle\,dV$. An $L^2$ realization means a complete real inner product space with a dense real-linear image of smooth sections preserving that integrated pairing, measurable representatives of finite squared norm, equality exactly when representatives agree almost everywhere, and every square-integrable measurable section represented. Its local distributions are the continuous real-linear functionals on scalar compactly supported smooth chart tests, valued in the model fibre, whose value is the integral of the test times the frame coefficients; the family of local distributions is injective. A Sobolev realization means a complete real inner product space with a dense real-linear image of smooth sections having exactly the order-$k$ energy as squared norm, and a bounded injective map to the $L^2$ realization agreeing with the identity on smooth sections. An elliptic differential operator consists of a real-linear map on smooth sections, smooth matrix coefficients in every pair of compatible charts and frames over the same chart, the local formula $Qs=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq k}b_\alpha\partial^\alpha s$, and bijectivity of $\sum_{|\alpha|=k}\xi^\alpha b_\alpha$ for every nonzero real covector. The distributional equation for two $L^2$ realizations is the componentwise identity against every scalar compactly supported smooth chart test $\phi$: the output pairing equals $\sum_{\alpha,l}(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int u_l\partial^\alpha(\phi b_{\alpha,jl})$. These are specifications of completions and canonical maps, with no existence assertion in the definitions. Empty index sums and rank-zero fibres are allowed.
